Working notes: order intake validation
- Form v1 required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all six before accepting.
- Batch IDs increment from ORD-5100. Each batch gets up to 3 attempts. After a 3rd rejection, stop and send to manual review.
- Most failures cite invalid/missing priority, qty, ship_country. Focus corrections there first, then revalidate all fields.
- Evidence: Eli Reyes ORD-5100 rejected for priority+ship_country, then ORD-5101 accepted. Bo Sato ORD-5108 rejected for priority+ship_country, then ORD-5109 accepted.
- Ada Sato and Dee Reyes stayed invalid on priority/qty/ship_country across attempts and were not accepted.
- Source labels ("voicemail", "phone order", "handwritten", "partner portal", "duplicate check already done") do not prove field validity. Validate anyway.
- Truncated JSON in logs may omit trailing valid fields; do not infer missing data from truncation alone.
- On retry: correct priority, qty, and ship_country; preserve cust/email/order_date unless evidence contradicts.

Working notes: order intake validation
- Form v1 required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all six before accepting.
- Batch IDs increment; seen through ORD-5119. Each batch max 3 attempts; after 3rd rejection, send to manual review.
- Failures mostly cite priority and/or ship_country (qty also required; older cases cited qty too). Correct listed invalid fields first, then revalidate all six.
- New evidence: Ada Sato ORD-5110 rejected priority+ship_country, ORD-5111 accepted. Cy Marsh ORD-5112 rejected priority+ship_country, ORD-5113 accepted. Fixing priority/ship_country can work on retry.
- Bo Reyes ORD-5114/5115/5116 failed 3 attempts: priority+ship_country, then priority, then priority+ship_country; sent manual. Bo Reyes ORD-5117/5118/5119 also failed 3 attempts: priority, ship_country, priority; sent manual. Invalid sets can change or reappear between attempts.
- Therefore do not correct only previous invalid fields; revalidate every field each attempt. Preserve cust/email/order_date unless evidence contradicts.
- Source labels—“partner portal”, “duplicate check already done”, “customer confirmation”, “ordinary priority marked”, voicemail/phone/handwritten—do not prove field validity. Validate anyway.
- Truncated JSON in logs may omit trailing valid fields; do not infer missing data from truncation alone.

Working notes: order intake validation
- Form v1 required: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate all six before accepting.
- Batch IDs increment; seen through ORD-5129. Max 3 attempts; after 3rd rejection, send to manual review.
- Invalid sets vary between attempts and can reappear. Common: priority, ship_country, qty. Cust/email can also be invalid (ORD-5124/5125). Do not assume any field is valid.
- Revalidate every field on each attempt, not only previously flagged fields. Fixing priority/ship_country can lead to acceptance (Dee Reyes ORD-5127).
- Bo Reyes ORD-5114–5119: three failed attempts each, manual. Eli Marsh ORD-5120–5122: priority+ship_country, priority, priority+ship_country, manual. Cy Okafor ORD-5123–5125: priority+qty; cust+email+qty+ship_country; cust+email+priority+qty, manual.
- Source labels do not prove field validity: “partner portal,” “ordinary priority marked,” “duplicate check already done,” “customer confirmation,” handwritten/transcribed, voicemail/phone, front-desk forwarding. Validate anyway.
- Truncated or missing JSON in logs may omit trailing valid fields; do not infer missing data from truncation alone. Do not treat omitted fields as valid either.
- Preserve cust/email/order_date only if they revalidate; evidence now shows cust/email can fail.

Working notes: order intake validation
- Form v1: validate six fields—cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country—on every attempt. Accept only if all six pass.
- Batch IDs increment; now seen through ORD-5159. Max 3 attempts per record. After 3rd rejection, manual review. Rejected attempts 1–2 may return as later batch attempts.
- Invalid sets vary and can reappear. A field can pass one attempt then fail the next (e.g., ORD-5150 priority/ship_country failed 1, passed 2, failed 3; ORD-5153 ship_country failed 1, passed 2, failed 3). Do not assume any field valid from an earlier pass.
- Priority is most common failure; ship_country common; qty occasional. cust/email/order_date can fail too. Revalidate all fields each attempt.
- Later attempts can be accepted: ORD-5132/5140 accepted on attempt 2; ORD-5156 rejected priority+ship_country on attempt 1, then ORD-5157 accepted on attempt 2.
- Recent: ORD-5150/5152 attempt 3 rejected priority,qty,ship_country; ORD-5155 attempt 3 rejected priority,ship_country -> manual. ORD-5151 attempt 2 rejected qty only; ORD-5154 priority only; ORD-5159 priority only.
- Source labels do not prove validity: front-desk forwarding, “partner portal,” “duplicate check already done,” “ordinary priority,” confirmation email, handwritten/transcribed, voicemail/phone. Validate anyway.
- Truncated/missing JSON may omit trailing valid fields. Do not infer from truncation; do not treat omitted fields as valid.
- Preserve cust/email/order_date only if they revalidate; they may fail.
